summary: NISAR FloodWatch is an interactive geospatial web application dashboard designed to monitor, track, and visualize global Earth surface changes and flood events using high-resolution NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite data. Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, the application processes radar imaging metrics to detect water body expansion, evaluate inundation extents, and provide timely insights into hydrological shifts. By combining advanced satellite remote sensing with an intuitive user interface, NISAR FloodWatch equips emergency responders, researchers, and local communities with critical visibility into environmental hazards, helping mitigate disaster risks and support proactive flood management.
details:
• Project Overview NISAR FloodWatch is a 24/7 satellite radar intelligence and flood-monitoring web platform built to eliminate the blind spots left by cloud cover during catastrophic monsoon floods. Designed for disaster response agencies, emergency planners, and vulnerable communities, the platform harnesses NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) L-band microwave observations to detect surface water expansion, map submerged infrastructure, and translate raw radar backscatter metrics into actionable community impact reports in near real time.

The Problem We Solve During peak monsoon seasons in low-lying regions such as Bangladesh’s Surma-Kushiyara (Sylhet & Sunamganj) basin and the Jamuna River floodplain, dense storm clouds render over 70% of traditional optical satellite imagery unusable. First responders and relief organizations are forced to operate blind—unable to track floodwater trajectories, locate severed bridges, or prioritize boat evacuations while waiting days for manual satellite analysis.

How It Works & Scientific Foundation Unlike optical sensors that rely on reflected sunlight and cannot penetrate clouds, NISAR transmits L-band microwave pulses (~24 cm wavelength) that pass straight through torrential rain and thick storm clouds day and night:

  • Specular Reflection & Backscatter Detection: Calm, open floodwater acts like a smooth mirror, reflecting radar pulses away from the sensor and producing a distinct radar backscatter drop of -9 to -11 dB compared to rough dry terrain.
  • Automated Water Segmentation & Vectorization: FloodWatch isolates these low-backscatter zones, compares them against pre-flood dry baselines, and converts inundation boundaries into interactive vector map layers.

Key Platform Features

  • Interactive Before-and-After Split Curtain Slider: Allows emergency responders to physically wipe between pre-flood dry baselines and peak inundation imagery across high-risk regions (including the Sylhet & Sunamganj Basin, Kurigram Jamuna River, Dhaka, and international benchmarks like Valencia) to spot breached riverbanks and flooded settlements immediately.
  • Multi-Layer GIS & Infrastructure Overlays: Toggles high-resolution satellite basemaps alongside critical infrastructure layers to pinpoint submerged road networks, severed bridges, isolated rural health clinics, and densely populated villages requiring urgent evacuation.
  • Flood Severity Analytics Dashboard: Quantifies total inundated area (sq km), water-level progression, severity ratings, and population/crop exposure metrics.
  • Built-In AI Damage & Vulnerability Assistant: Translates complex microwave decibel (dB) thresholds and spatial overlays into clear, plain-language damage assessments and evacuation summaries for non-technical field coordinators.
  • Interactive Story Mode: Animates the chronological flood timeline from initial heavy rainfall to peak crest and recession, helping planners understand flood dynamics and historical recurrence.
  • Modular Data Provider Architecture & One-Click Export: Engineered with a scalable DataProvider interface ready to ingest live NASA Earthdata CMR and ASF DAAC data streams, plus one-click structured JSON assessment exports for seamless inter-agency coordination.

Future Roadmap & Global Impact

  • Water Depth Simulation: Integrating Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) with radar-derived flood extents to estimate localized water depth across urban and agricultural zones.
  • Automated Last-Mile Early Warnings: Connecting threshold alerts directly to automated SMS and community broadcast pipelines so remote villages receive timely evacuation notices before roads are cut off.
